sections.text:
**LLM readability** refers to how easily large language models can parse, understand, and extract information from your content[6]. The higher the LLM readability, the more likely it is that content will be extracted and cited by AI systems such as Google AI Mode, ChatGPT, or Perplexity[1].

LLM readability differs from traditional human readability because LLMs don't interpret content visually. Instead, they convert plain text into structured pieces and use those pieces to locate information through processes like tokenization, chunking based on semantic similarity, and embedding and vector retrieval[5].

The seven core factors that influence LLM readability are: natural language quality, structuring, chunk relevance, user intent match, information hierarchy, context management, and consistency and specificity[1]. Measurable indicators of good LLM readability include the percentage of question-based headings, average paragraph length (ideally under 400 characters), consistency of core terminology, and the presence of explicit answer types like numbers, data, and entities[1].

One approach to improving LLM readability is implementing **LLMs.txt**, a new web standard that provides content in a plain-text, structured format using Markdown, making it easier for AI to access and process key information without dealing with unnecessary web elements[4].
